column1: # asktimeout-fields.tsv: the inventory of every ledger field the classifier of scripts/ask-timeout.sh reads (the list and the claim/record modes' own reads of filesAt, verdictRef and issue are bash-level and listed in the script header).
# NOT seen by the static check, by design: the claim mode reads asks.*.filesAt (and noCode) in its own small jq program in bash, not in the classifier,
# so the compiled-program seam never lists it. Its wrong-type behaviour is pinned by the AT-F rows of scripts/test/ask-timeout.sh (a non-text or unparseable
# filesAt is never fresh: claim refused, exit 2). A new classifier read still needs a line here.

# One line per field path: doc (led, the ledger), path (dotted; * is any one key or index), the legal JSON types besides null (jq type names; null is always legal), a class, the bases (A = at-a, B = at-b of scripts/test/ask-timeout-base.sh: where a wrong value is protective), a note. Class:

#   A  a wrong type there decides whether an ask is delegated to the concertmaster at all: it must never read as absent, never be coerced to text, and the ask is never verdict-due (never, or not an open ask)
#   B  time only: a wrong value is ignored while timeoutAt stands, and an ask with neither never times out: never a verdict
